# PR #3990: Patch: the Worker alerts when the game server won't start or can't be reached

Closes #3618

The Worker now raises `server.unreachable` itself. It fires when a request's container start throws or outruns `START_WAIT_MS`, and when the daily cron's `/readyz` fails. The edge tests, typecheck and eslint pass, and the build needs no new secret or var. The staging check from the issue's "Done when" is not done: it needs staging's secrets and Cloudflare, so it is for a person after the deploy.

## What changed

- **`apps/edge/src/alerts.ts` (new):** a fetch-based port of `crates/server/src/alerts.rs`, with the same title, labels, email wording and `Idempotency-Key` scheme (per new issue, else per site and UTC day).
  - `tell` searches for an open issue with exactly the title `Patch: alert server.unreachable on <site>`. If one exists it comments; otherwise it opens one with the `architecture` and `human` labels.
  - It emails `ALERT_EMAILS` through Resend unless a comment carried the notice.
  - The issue and comment hold no field values, since the repository is public. The cause goes only in the email and the Worker's logs.
  - Resend's 409 counts as already sent. A failed step is logged and never throws. Tokens, keys and addresses are never logged.
- **`apps/edge/src/index.ts`:**
  - `awaitStart`'s catch calls `ctx.waitUntil(this.tellUnreachable(...))`, so the player's request never waits for a send. A client that hung up (`signal.aborted`) raises nothing.
  - The new public method `tellUnreachable` is also what the cron calls over Durable Object RPC. It never rejects.
  - `claimNotice` keeps when it last told in Durable Object storage under `jackioh:server.unreachable:toldAt`, so a boot loop tells once an hour.
  - `claimNotice` sets the in-memory time before it awaits the storage write. Requests that fail on the same boot fail together, so the one that wins the claim is the only one that tells.
  - `scheduled(controller, env, ctx)` alerts on a non-ok or throwing `/readyz`, then still throws the same message the existing test holds. The hourly sweep is unchanged and raises no alert.
- **`apps/edge/src/network.fake.ts` (new):** a GitHub and Resend fake shared by both test files, left out of Stryker in `stryker.config.mjs`.
- **Docs:** `apps/edge/README.md` (a behaviour bullet, and the Worker now reads the three secrets), `crates/server/README.md` (the "next steps" sentence now points at the Worker's alert), and `docs/deploy-cloudflare.md` (the "An alert" and "The server will not start" bullets, with the staging check).

## Tests I ran

- `pnpm exec vitest run --project edge`: 4 files, 115 tests pass.
- `pnpm --dir apps/edge typecheck`: clean.
- `pnpm exec eslint apps/edge`: exit 0.
- Two mutation checks on `index.ts`:
  - Removing the in-memory `this.toldAt = now` made 4 tests fail.
  - Removing the `signal.aborted` guard made the "client that hung up" test fail.
- The web vitest files that read `apps/edge` (`cloudflare-config.test.ts`, `ci-scope.test.ts`) could not load here, because `apps/web/src/wasm/pkg` is not built. The harness runs `scripts/build-wasm.sh` first. No Rust, spec or catalog files changed.

## Decisions the issue did not settle

- **No held-count in the notice.** Counting suppressed alerts would mean a storage write on every failing request.
- **No per-day email cap beyond the idempotency key.** The server caps at `ALERT_EMAILS_PER_DAY`; here the hourly window plus the key already bound it to one email per issue or one per day. I rejected a second counter in storage.
- **The hourly sweep does not alert.** The issue names only the daily `/readyz`.
- **A client that hung up is not an alert.** Its abort ends the start wait and is no fault of the server.
- **Departures from the plan:**
  - `github()` takes the token as its first argument.
  - `claimNotice` survives a storage read or write failure (a read failure counts as never told, a write failure costs at most a repeat) and logs `server.alert_state_unreadable` or `server.alert_state_unwritten`. I chose that because alerting despite broken storage beats saying nothing.
  - `TOLD_AT_KEY` is exported so a test can read it.

## Worth a second look

- `claimNotice` is the part the tests exercise least realistically: a real Durable Object's input gates and `ctx.waitUntil` (documented as a no-op there) are only faked.
- A failed start inside the cron's own `/readyz` fetch tells once from `awaitStart`. The cron's `tellUnreachable` call then lands inside the same window and tells nothing. A test (`tells people through the object the request path uses…`) holds that.

# #3618: Patch: the Worker alerts when the game server won't start or can't be reached
Opened by @jgoetzmann.

@MaxGoetzmann is this worth building? Comment `approve` to have the night bot build it, or `reject` to close it.

### Why

#3595 has the server tell people about its own alerts: a GitHub issue and an email. A server that cannot start, or that the Worker cannot reach, can tell nobody. Two cases:

- **The server won't boot.** `release` exits on a failed migration or catalog seed (docs/deploy-cloudflare.md section 5, "The server will not start"). With one container there is no older one to keep serving.
- **The server boots too slowly.** On 2026-11-04 the first visitor after a sleep got a 500, because the server took longer than the Worker's wait. The server never saw that request at all.

Today either one is found when a player says the site is down.

### What

In `apps/edge`, the Worker raises its own alert, `server.unreachable`, when:

- a request finds the container failed to start or not answering within `START_WAIT_MS`, or
- the daily cron's `/readyz` fails.

It then:

- tells people the way `crates/server/src/alerts.rs` does: an issue `Patch: alert server.unreachable on <site>` (`architecture`, `human`), through `CREATE_ISSUES_TOKEN`, and an email through Resend to `ALERT_EMAILS`. The Worker already holds all three secrets, so a person sets nothing new;
- uses the same Resend `Idempotency-Key` scheme (per new issue, else per event, site and day), so it never spends the 100 emails a day the sign-in mail shares;
- keeps when it last told in its Durable Object's storage, so a server failing on every request alerts once, not once a request;
- sends from `ctx.waitUntil`, never while the player's request waits.

### Done when

- `apps/edge` tests, with GitHub and Resend faked, cover each case: one issue and one email for a boot loop, a comment once an issue is open, and nothing within the window.
- On staging, a forced boot failure opens one issue and sends one email.

Follows #3595.

     ```ts

     await this.toldAtLoad;
     if (now - this.toldAt < ALERT_WINDOW_MS) return false;

     return true;

- `siteOf` gives `jackioh.com` for `https://jackioh.com`, `staging.jackioh.com` for `https://staging.jackioh.com/`, the first of two comma-separated origins, and `an unnamed site` for `undefined`.

  - "opens a new issue and emails again once it is closed": at the window with an empty search, a second issue POST and a Resend POST with the new URL's key.
  - "remembers across a restart": a second `Server` on the same fake storage inside the window tells nothing.
  - "makes one notice for requests that fail together": two requests in `Promise.all`, one issue POST.
  - "sends from waitUntil, not while the request waits": the fake `fetch` never resolves, yet `await server.fetch(request())` resolves with the answer and `waitUntil` was called once.
